**Finding: Deviation (AUDIT) — § 11.3 Suspected Violations**

- **Issue:** § 11.3 (p0132) grants IBM an open-ended right to "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty, with no frequency cap, no advance notice (p0137 only promises attempted notice before restricting access/removing Content), no independent-auditor or confidentiality condition, no cost allocation, and no bar on accessing Customer systems. p0138 compounds this by requiring us to supply all relevant information on request. That is the playbook's walk-away scenario.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** new paragraph after p0137 limiting any investigation requiring access to our records, facilities or systems to once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours without unreasonable disruption, by an independent auditor under confidentiality, remote/off-site where practicable with no direct access to Customer systems or Customer Components, and at IBM's expense unless an underpayment exceeds 5%.
- **Fallback if pushed:** 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold.
